english.title: Obstruct a person exercising a power of entry - Private Security Industry Act 2001
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intentionally obstructed a person authorised in writing by the Private Security Industry Authority, namely **(..SPECIFY NAME..), in the exercise of a power under section 19(1) of the Private Security Industry Act 2001 to enter premises situated at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION OF THE PREMISES..) owned or occupied by a person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), who appeared to that authorised person to be a person regulated by the Act
english.legislation: Contrary to section 19(5)(a) and (7) of the Private Security Industry Act 2001.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale

Time limit for prosecutions:
Six months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
